definitions.explanation: A cooking method in which food is cooked by steam. Also used as a prefix to describe steamed dishes.

examples.japanese: {蒸|む}し⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ヘルシーだ。
{茶碗|ちゃわん}{蒸|む}し⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{代表的|だいひょうてき}→代表的：05670_daihyouteki⟧な{蒸|む}し⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧だ。
examples.english: Chawanmushi is a representative Japanese steamed dish.
I think steaming fish rather than grilling it brings out the natural flavor of the ingredients.

notes:
{蒸|む}し refers to the steaming method of cooking. It is derived from the verb ⟦{蒸|む}す→蒸す：02307_musu⟧ (to steam). This is distinct from ⟦{虫|むし}→虫：02262_mushi⟧ (insect) and ⟦{無視|むし}→無視：13473_mushi⟧ (ignoring), which share the same reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {蒸|む}し⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧ (steamed dishes)
- {蒸|む}し{器|き} (steamer)
- {蒸|む}し{鶏|どり} (steamed chicken)
- {蒸|む}し⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧ (steamed vegetables)

COMMON STEAMED DISHES:
- {茶碗|ちゃわん}{蒸|む}し (egg custard steamed in a cup)
- {酒|さか}{蒸|む}し (sake-steamed)
- {蒸|む}し⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧ (steamed bread/bun)

Steaming is one of the fundamental cooking techniques in Japanese cuisine, valued for preserving the natural flavors and nutrients of ingredients.
